patch_description:
Analysis of the three prior variants shows the score plateaus at 0.80 whenever n_params=8 (1 shared trainable parameter "theta" per repetition) and accuracy is already perfect (1.0) across train/val/test with zero generalization gap. This implies parameter_efficiency ≈ accuracy/n_params is the dominant score driver, and since we're already at the minimal nonzero parameter floor (1 unique name × fixed repetition count), adding a second parameter (as suggested by the naive "two thetas" recommendation) would double n_params and likely hurt parameter efficiency without any accuracy gain (accuracy is already saturated at 1.0).

Instead, I simplify the block to reduce depth and gate count while keeping exactly one shared parameter name "theta", mirroring the leanest-performing seed (which had the lowest validation/test loss, 0.01, at depth 84 and gate count 168) but retaining the antipodal long-range connectivity that seemed to help convergence speed (60 steps) in the current version. Concretely, I drop the redundant "skip-2" fixed CZ layer (2b) since it adds gate count/depth without touching parameter count or without clear benefit over the plain ring + antipodal connections, keeping the circuit shallower and hopefully converging faster and generalizing at least as well, which may nudge the secondary score terms (loss, convergence, depth) upward without risking the already-saturated accuracy or the parameter-economy floor.
